children.text: Chapter 1
athāto himaśailāgre devadāruvanālaye
children.translated_text: Now, long ago, on the summit of the snowy mountain, in a dwelling in the deodar forest,

children.text: vyāsam ekāgram āsīnam apṛcchann ṛṣayaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: the sages questioned <s>Vyāsa</s>, who was seated with one-pointed mind.

children.text: mānuṣāṇāṃ hitaṃ dharmaṃ vartamāne kalau yuge
children.translated_text: "Tell us the beneficial <s>dharma</s> (religious law) for human beings in the present Kali age,

children.text: śaucācāraṃ yathāvac ca vada satyavatīsuta ||
children.translated_text: and purity and conduct as they truly are, O son of <s>Satyavatī</s>."

children.text: tacchrutvā ṛṣivākyaṃ tu saśiṣyo 'gnyarkasaṃnibhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the sages, he, together with his disciples, radiant like fire and the sun,

children.text: pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ śrutismṛtiviśāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the greatly splendid one, skilled in śruti and smṛti, replied:

children.text: na cāhaṃ sarvatattvajñaḥ kathaṃ dharmaṃ vadāmy ahaṃ
children.translated_text: "I am not a knower of all principles. How could I state the <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: asmatpitaiva praṣṭavya iti vyāsaḥ suto 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: My own father should be asked." Thus spoke <s>Vyāsa</s>, the son.

children.text: tatas ta ṛṣayaḥ sarve dharmatattvārthakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then all those sages, desiring the meaning of the principle of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: ṛṣiṃ vyāsaṃ puraskṛtya gatā badarikāśramam ||
children.translated_text: placed the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> at their head and went to <s>Badarikāśrama</s>.

children.text: nānāpuṣpalatākīrṇaṃ phalavṛkṣair alaṃkṛtam
children.translated_text: It was strewn with many flowers and creepers, adorned with fruit trees,

children.text: nadīprasravaṇopetaṃ puṇyatīrthopaśobhitaṃ ||
children.translated_text: endowed with rivers and springs, and beautified by holy bathing places.

children.text: mṛgapakṣininādāḍhyaṃ devatāyatanāvṛtam
children.translated_text: It abounded in the calls of deer and birds and was surrounded by shrines of the gods,

children.text: yakṣagandharvasiddhaiś ca nṛtyagītair alaṃkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and it was adorned by yakṣas, gandharvas, and siddhas with dancing and songs.

children.text: tasminn ṛṣisabhāmadhye śaktiputraṃ parāśaram
children.translated_text: There, in the midst of an assembly of sages, they saw <s>Parāśara</s>, the son of <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: sukhāsīnaṃ mahātejā munimukhyagaṇāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the greatly splendid sage, seated comfortably and surrounded by groups of foremost seers.

children.text: kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā vyāsas tu ṛṣibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vyāsa</s>, together with the sages, folding his hands in reverence,

children.text: pradakṣiṇābhivādaiś ca stutibhiḥ samapūjayat ||
children.translated_text: honored him with circumambulations, salutations, and hymns of praise.

children.text: tataḥ saṃtuṣṭahṛdayaḥ parāśaramahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Then the great sage <s>Parāśara</s>, his heart pleased,

children.text: āha susvāgataṃ brūhīty āsīno munipuṅgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, while seated, "Welcome indeed; speak," O best of sages.

children.text: kuśalaṃ samyag ity uktvā vyāsaḥ pṛcchaty anantaram
children.translated_text: After saying, "All is well," <s>Vyāsa</s> then asked:

children.text: yadi jānāsi bhaktiṃ me snehād vā bhaktavatsala ||
children.translated_text: "If you know my devotion, or from affection for me, O lover of your devotees,

children.text: dharmaṃ kathaya me tāta anugrāhyo hy ahaṃ tava
children.translated_text: teach me <s>dharma</s>, father; for I am one to be favored by you.

children.text: śrutā me mānavā dharmā vāsiṣṭhāḥ kāśyapās tathā ||
children.translated_text: I have heard the human dharmas, and those of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> too,

children.text: gārgeyā gautamīyāś ca tathā cośanasā smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: those of <s>Garga</s> and <s>Gautama</s>, and likewise those remembered as belonging to <s>Uśanas</s>,

children.text: atrer viṣṇoś ca saṃvartād dakṣād aṅgirasas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and those of <s>Atri</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> as well.

children.text: śātātapāc ca hārītād yājñavalkyāt tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: I have heard those from <s>Śātātapa</s> and <s>Hārīta</s>, and likewise from <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,

children.text: āpastambakṛtā dharmāḥ śaṅkhasya likhitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the dharmas composed by <s>Āpastamba</s>, and those of <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Likhita</s>,

children.text: kātyāyanakṛtāś caiva tathā prācetasān muneḥ
children.translated_text: those composed by <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and likewise those of the sage <s>Prācetasa</s>.

children.text: śrutā hy ete bhavatproktāḥ śrutyarthā me na vismṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All these, taught by you, have indeed been heard by me; the meanings of śruti have not been forgotten by me.

children.text: asmin manvantare dharmāḥ kṛtatretādike yuge
children.translated_text: In this manvantara, the dharmas in the Kṛta, Tretā, and other ages

children.text: sarve dharmāḥ kṛte jātāḥ sarve naṣṭāḥ kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: all arose in the Kṛta age, but all are lost in the Kali age.

children.text: cāturvarṇyasamācāraṃ kiṃcit sādhāraṇaṃ vada
children.translated_text: Tell something common regarding the conduct of the four varṇas,

children.text: caturṇām api varṇānāṃ kartavyaṃ dharmakovidaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the duty to be performed by all four varṇas, as understood by knowers of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: brūhi dharmasvarūpajña sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ ca vistarāt
children.translated_text: Speak at length, O knower of the nature of <s>dharma</s>, both of the subtle and of the gross."

children.text: vyāsavākyāvasāne tu munimukhyaḥ parāśaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of <s>Vyāsa</s>'s words, the foremost sage <s>Parāśara</s>

children.text: dharmasya nirṇayaṃ prāha sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ ca vistarāt
children.translated_text: declared the determination of <s>dharma</s>, both subtle and gross, in detail:

children.text: śṛṇu putra pravakṣyāmi śṛṇvantu munayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: "Listen, my son, I shall explain it; let the sages also listen.

children.text: kalpe kalpe kṣayotpattyā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: In each kalpa, through dissolution and creation, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>

children.text: śrutismṛtisadācāranirṇetāraś ca sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: are always the determiners of śruti, smṛti, and good custom.

children.text: na kaścid vedakartā ca vedaṃ smṛtvā caturmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: No one is a maker of the Veda; the four-faced one remembers the Veda,

children.text: tathaiva dharmān smarati manuḥ kalpāntare 'ntare ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Manu</s> remembers the dharmas in each successive kalpa.

children.text: anye kṛtayuge dharmās tretāyāṃ dvāpare yuge
children.translated_text: The dharmas are different in the Kṛta age, in Tretā, and in Dvāpara,

children.text: anye kaliyuge nṝṇāṃ yugarūpānusārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and different for human beings in the Kali age, according to the form of the age.

children.text: tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānam ucyate
children.translated_text: Austerity is supreme in the Kṛta age; in Tretā, knowledge is said to be supreme.

children.text: dvāpare yajñam evāhuḥ dānam eva kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara they call sacrifice supreme; in the Kali age, charity alone.

children.text: kṛte tu mānavā dharmās tretāyāṃ gautamāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: In Kṛta the dharmas of <s>Manu</s> are remembered; in Tretā, those of <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: dvāpare śāṅkhalikhitāḥ kalau pārāśarāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara, those of <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Likhita</s>; in Kali, those of <s>Parāśara</s> are remembered.

children.text: tyajed deśaṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ grāmam utsṛjet
children.translated_text: In the Kṛta age one should abandon a country; in Tretā one should leave a village.

children.text: dvāpare kulam ekaṃ tu kartāraṃ tu kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara one family only, but in the Kali age the perpetrator alone should be abandoned.

children.text: kṛte saṃbhāṣaṇād eva tretāyāṃ sparśanena ca
children.translated_text: In Kṛta one falls merely by conversation; in Tretā, by touch.

children.text: dvāpare tv annam ādāya kalau patati karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara, by accepting food; in Kali one falls by the act itself.

children.text: kṛte tātkālikaḥ śāpas tretāyāṃ daśabhir dinaiḥ
children.translated_text: In Kṛta a curse takes effect immediately; in Tretā, after ten days.

children.text: dvāpare caikamāsena kalau saṃvatsareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara, after one month; in Kali, after a year.

children.text: abhigamya kṛte dānaṃ tretāsv āhūya dīyate
children.translated_text: In Kṛta a gift is given by going to the recipient; in Tretā it is given after inviting him.

children.text: dvāpare yācamānāya sevayā dīyate kalau ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara it is given to one who asks; in Kali it is given in return for service.

children.text: abhigamyottamaṃ dānam āhūyaiva tu madhyamam
children.translated_text: A gift made by going to the recipient is the best; one made after inviting him is middling.

children.text: adhamaṃ yācamānāya sevādānaṃ tu niṣphalam ||
children.translated_text: A gift to one who asks is inferior, while a gift for service is fruitless.

children.text: jito dharmo hy adharmeṇa satyaṃ caivānṛtena ca
children.translated_text: In Kali, <s>dharma</s> has been conquered by adharma, and truth by falsehood;

children.text: jitāś coraiś ca rājānaḥ strībhiś ca puruṣāḥ kalau ||
children.translated_text: kings have been conquered by thieves, and men by women.

children.text: sīdanti cāgnihotrāṇi gurupūjā praṇaśyati
children.translated_text: Agnihotras decline, and reverence for the teacher perishes;

children.text: kumāryaś ca prasūyante asmin kaliyuge sadā ||
children.translated_text: maidens give birth continually in this Kali age.

children.text: kṛte tv asthigatāḥ prāṇās tretāyāṃ māṃsam āśritāḥ
children.translated_text: In Kṛta, life-breaths were located in the bones; in Tretā, they depended on flesh.

children.text: dvāpare rudhiraṃ caiva kalau tv annādiṣu sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara, on blood; but in Kali they are situated in food and the like.

children.text: yuge yuge ca ye dharmās tatra tatra ca ye dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: In each age, whatever the dharmas are, and whatever twice-born men are present there,

children.text: teṣāṃ nindā na kartavyā yugarūpā hi te dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are not to be blamed, for those twice-born men conform to the form of the age.

children.text: yuge yuge tu sāmarthyaṃ śeṣaṃ munivibhāṣitam
children.translated_text: In each age, what capacity remains has been explained by sages;

children.text: parāśareṇa cāpy uktaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and by <s>Parāśara</s> too atonement is prescribed.

children.text: aham adyaiva tat sarvam anusmṛtya bravīmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: Today I shall recall all that and tell it to you.

children.text: cāturvarṇyasamācāraṃ śṛṇvantu ṛṣipuṅgavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the foremost sages listen to the conduct of the four varṇas.

children.text: parāśaramataṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam
children.translated_text: The opinion of <s>Parāśara</s> is meritorious, purifying, and destructive of sin;

children.text: cintitaṃ brāhmaṇārthāya dharmasaṃsthāpanāya ca ||
children.translated_text: it has been considered for the sake of brāhmaṇas and for the establishment of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: caturṇām api varṇānām ācāro dharmapālakaḥ
children.translated_text: For all four varṇas, conduct is the protector of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ācārabhraṣṭadehānāṃ bhaved dharmaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those whose bodies have fallen away from proper conduct, <s>dharma</s> turns its face away.

children.text: ṣaṭkarmābhirato nityaṃ devatātithipūjakaḥ
children.translated_text: A brāhmaṇa who is always devoted to the six duties and worships deities and guests,

children.text: hutaśeṣaṃ tu bhuñjāno brāhmaṇo nāvasīdati ||
children.translated_text: and who eats what remains after the oblation, does not sink down."

children.text: saṃdhyāsnānaṃ japo homo devatātithipūjanam
children.translated_text: Twilight worship, bathing, recitation, oblation, worship of deities and guests,

children.text: ātithyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca ṣaṭkarmāṇi dine dine ||
children.translated_text: hospitality and the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering: these are the six duties day by day.

children.text: iṣṭo vā yadi vā dveṣyo mūrkhaḥ paṇḍita eva vā
children.translated_text: Whether he is liked or disliked, foolish or indeed learned,

children.text: samprāpto vaiśvadevānte so 'tithiḥ svargasaṃgramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who has arrived at the end of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> is a guest, a passage to heaven.

children.text: dūrādhvopagataṃ śrāntaṃ vaiśvadeva upasthitam
children.translated_text: One should know as a guest the man who has come from a distant road, weary,

children.text: atithiṃ taṃ vijānīyān nātithiḥ pūrvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and has appeared at the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; one who has come earlier is not a guest.

children.text: naikagrāmīṇam atithiṃ saṃgṛhṇīta kadācana
children.translated_text: One should never take as a guest someone from the same village,

children.text: anityam āgato yasmāt tasmād atithir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: for because he has come without permanence, therefore he is called an <s>atithi</s> (guest).

children.text: atithiṃ tatra samprāptaṃ pūjayet svāgatādinā
children.translated_text: When a guest has arrived there, one should honor him with words of welcome and the like,

children.text: arghyāsanapradānena pādaprakṣālanena ca ||
children.translated_text: with the giving of arghya-water and a seat, and with washing of the feet,

children.text: śraddhayā cānnadānena priyapraśnottareṇa ca
children.translated_text: with the faithful giving of food, and with pleasant questions and replies;

children.text: gacchantaṃ cānuyānena prītim utpādayed gṛhī ||
children.translated_text: and, when he goes, by following him a little, the householder should produce affection.

children.text: atithir yasya bhagnāśo gṛhāt pratinivartate
children.translated_text: If a guest returns from someone's house with his hopes broken,

children.text: pitaras tasya nāśnanti daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: that man's ancestors do not eat for fifteen years.

children.text: kāṣṭhabhārasahasreṇa ghṛtakumbhaśatena ca
children.translated_text: For the one whose guest's hopes are broken, even with a thousand loads of wood

children.text: atithir yasya bhagnāśas tasya homo nirarthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a hundred jars of ghee, his fire-offering is useless.

children.text: sukṣetre vāpayed bījaṃ supātre nikṣiped dhanam
children.translated_text: One should sow seed in good soil, and deposit wealth in a worthy vessel;

children.text: sukṣetre ca supātre ca hy uptaṃ dattaṃ na naśyati ||
children.translated_text: what is sown in good soil and given to a worthy vessel does not perish.

children.text: na pṛcched gotracaraṇe na svādhyāyaṃ śrutaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: One should not ask about his lineage or school, nor likewise about the Veda-study he has heard;

children.text: hṛdaye kalpayed devaṃ sarvadevamayo hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should imagine him in one's heart as a god, for he consists of all the gods.

children.text: apūrvaḥ suvratī vipro hy apūrvaś cātithir yathā
children.translated_text: A Brahmin who keeps good vows is unprecedented, just as a guest is unprecedented;

children.text: vedābhyāsarato nityaṃ tāv apūrvau dine dine ||
children.translated_text: being constantly devoted to Vedic study, those two are unprecedented day by day.

children.text: vaiśvadeve tu samprāpte bhikṣuke gṛham āgate
children.translated_text: But when, at the time of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, a beggar has come to the house,

children.text: uddhṛtya vaiśvadevārthaṃ bhikṣukaṃ tu visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: one should set aside what is for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and then send the beggar away.

children.text: yatiś ca brahmacārī ca pakvānnasvāmināv ubhau
children.translated_text: An ascetic and a celibate student are both masters of cooked food;

children.text: tayor annam adattvā tu bhuktvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: if one eats without giving them food, one should perform the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> penance.

children.text: dadyāc ca bhikṣātritayaṃ parivrāḍ brahmacāriṇām
children.translated_text: One should give three alms-portions to wandering ascetics and celibate students,

children.text: icchayā ca tato dadyād vibhave satyavāritam ||
children.translated_text: and after that one may give as one wishes, without being restrained, if there is means.

children.text: yatihaste jalaṃ dadyād bhaikṣaṃ dadyāt punar jalam
children.translated_text: One should give water into the ascetic's hand, then give alms, and again water;

children.text: tad bhaikṣyaṃ meruṇā tulyaṃ taj jalaṃ sāgaropamam ||
children.translated_text: those alms are equal to <s>Meru</s>, and that water is like the ocean.

children.text: yasya chatraṃ hayaś caiva kuñjarāroham ṛddhimat
children.translated_text: He whose umbrella, horse, and prosperous elephant-mount are present

children.text: aindraṃ sthānam upāsīta tasmāt taṃ na vicārayet ||
children.translated_text: would attain the station of <s>Indra</s>; therefore one should not examine him.

children.text: vaiśvadevakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śakto bhikṣur vyapohitum
children.translated_text: A capable beggar is able to remove the sin committed in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>;

children.text: na hi bhikṣukṛtān doṣān vaiśvadevo vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> does not remove faults committed against a beggar.

children.text: akṛtvā vaiśvadevaṃ tu bhuñjate ye dvijādhamāḥ
children.translated_text: Those lowest twice-born men who eat without performing the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>

children.text: sarve te niṣphalā jñeyāḥ patanti narake 'śucau ||
children.translated_text: should all be known as fruitless; they fall into an impure hell.

children.text: vaiśvadevavihīnā ye ātithyena bahiṣkṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are without the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and excluded from hospitality

children.text: sarve te narakaṃ yānti kākayoniṃ vrajanti ca ||
children.translated_text: all go to hell and are born in the wombs of crows.

children.text: pāpo vā yadi caṇḍālo vipraghnaḥ pitṛghātakaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether he is sinful, or a Caṇḍāla, a Brahmin-killer, or a father-killer,

children.text: vaiśvadeve tu samprāptaḥ so 'tithiḥ svargasaṃkramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if he has arrived at the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, he is a guest, a passage to heaven.

children.text: yo veṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yo bhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: One who eats with his head wrapped, one who eats facing south,

children.text: vāmapāde karaṃ nyasya tad vai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate ||
children.translated_text: or placing his hand on his left foot: that food the demons indeed eat.

children.text: avratā hy anadhīyānā yatra bhaikṣacarā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Where twice-born men who are without vows and do not study go about begging,

children.text: taṃ grāmaṃ daṇḍayed rājā corabhaktaprado hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should punish that village, for it is a giver of food to thieves.

children.text: kṣatriyo hi prajā rakṣañ śastrapāṇiḥ pradaṇḍavān
children.translated_text: A Kṣatriya, protecting his subjects, armed with a weapon and bearing the rod of punishment,

children.text: nirjitya parasainyāni kṣitiṃ dharmeṇa pālayet ||
children.translated_text: should conquer hostile armies and govern the earth according to <s>dharma</s> (lawful order).

children.text: puṣpaṃ puṣpaṃ vicinuyān mūlacchedaṃ na kārayet
children.translated_text: He should pluck flower after flower, but should not cause the root to be cut,

children.text: mālākāra ivārāme na yathāṅgārakārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a garland-maker in a garden, and not like a charcoal-maker.

children.text: lābhakarma tathā ratnaṃ gavāṃ ca paripālanam
children.translated_text: Works for profit, likewise jewels, the protection of cattle,

children.text: kṛṣikarma ca vāṇijyaṃ vaiśyavṛttir udāhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: agriculture and trade are declared to be a Vaiśya's occupation.

children.text: śūdrasya dvijaśuśrūṣā paramo dharma ucyate
children.translated_text: Service to the twice-born is called the highest <s>dharma</s> for a Śūdra;

children.text: anyathā kurute kiṃcit tad bhavet tasya niṣphalam ||
children.translated_text: if he does anything otherwise, that becomes fruitless for him.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ madhutailaṃ ca dadhitakraṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ
children.translated_text: Salt, honey, oil, curd, buttermilk, ghee, and milk

children.text: na duṣyecchūdrajātīnāṃ kuryāt sarveṣu vikrayam ||
children.translated_text: are not defiled by Śūdra-born people; one may make sale of them among all.

children.text: vikrīṇan madhyamāṃsāni hy abhakṣasya ca bhakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Selling liquor and meats, eating what is not to be eaten,

children.text: kurvann agamyāgamanaṃ śūdraḥ patati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and having intercourse with a forbidden woman, a Śūdra falls at once.

children.text: kapilākṣīrapānena brāhmaṇīgamanena ca
children.translated_text: By drinking the milk of a tawny cow, by going to a Brahmin woman,

children.text: vedākṣaravicāreṇa śūdraś cāṇḍālatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: and by examining the syllables of the Veda, a Śūdra becomes a Caṇḍāla.

children.text: Chapter 2
ataḥ paraṃ gṛhasthasya karmācāraṃ kalau yuge
children.translated_text: Hereafter, concerning the householder's conduct of acts in the Kali age,

children.text: dharmaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ śaktyā cāturvarṇyāśramāgatam ||
children.translated_text: the common <s>dharma</s>, according to ability, belonging to the four varṇas and āśramas,

children.text: taṃ pravakṣyāmy ahaṃ pūrvaṃ parāśaravaco yathā
children.translated_text: I shall declare it first, just as the speech of <s>Parāśara</s> says.

children.text: ṣaṭkarmasahito vipraḥ kṛṣikarma ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: A Brahmin, furnished with the six rites, may also have agricultural work done.

children.text: kṣudhitaṃ tṛṣitaṃ śrāntaṃ balīvardaṃ na yojayet
children.translated_text: He should not yoke an ox that is hungry, thirsty, or exhausted;

children.text: hīnāṅgaṃ vyādhitaṃ klībaṃ vṛṣaṃ vipro na vāhayet ||
children.translated_text: a Brahmin should not make pull a bull that is defective in limb, diseased, impotent, or castrated.

children.text: sthirāṅgaṃ nīrujaṃ tṛptaṃ sunardaṃ ṣaṇḍhavarjitam
children.translated_text: One that is firm-limbed, healthy, satisfied, strong-bellowing, and not castrated

children.text: vāhayed divasasyārdhaṃ paścāt snānaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: he may make pull for half the day; afterward he should perform bathing.

children.text: japyaṃ devārcanaṃ homaṃ svādhyāyaṃ caivam abhyaset
children.translated_text: He should practice recitation, worship of the gods, oblation, and private Vedic study in this way;

children.text: ekadvitricaturviprān bhojayet snātakān dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the twice-born man should feed one, two, three, or four initiated Brahmins.

children.text: svayaṃkṛṣṭe tathā kṣetre dhānyaiś ca svayamarjitaiḥ
children.translated_text: In a field ploughed by himself, and with grain acquired by himself,

children.text: nirvapet pañca yajñāṃś ca kratudīkṣāṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: he should perform the five sacrifices and undertake the consecration for sacrifice.

children.text: tilā rasā na vikreyā vikreyā dhānyatatsamāḥ
children.translated_text: Sesame seeds and liquids are not to be sold; grain and things equivalent to it may be sold.

children.text: viprasyaivaṃvidhā vṛttis tṛṇakāṣṭhādivikrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Such is a Brahmin's livelihood: the sale of grass, wood, and the like.

children.text: brāhmaṇaś cet kṛṣiṃ kuryāt tanmahādoṣam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: But if a Brahmin practices agriculture, he incurs that great fault

children.text: saṃvatsareṇa yat pāpaṃ matsyaghātī samāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: which a killer of fish obtains in a year.

children.text: ayomukhena kāṣṭhena tad ekāhena lāṅgalī
children.translated_text: With wood having an iron mouth, the ploughman obtains that in a single day.

children.text: pāśako matsyaghātī ca vyādhaḥ śākunikas tathā ||
children.translated_text: The gambler, the killer of fish, the hunter, and likewise the bird-catcher,

children.text: adātā karṣakaś caiva sarve te samabhāginaḥ
children.translated_text: the one who does not give, and the farmer too: all of these share equally in that fault.

children.text: vṛkṣaṃ chittvā mahīṃ bhittvā hatvā ca kṛmikīṭakān ||
children.translated_text: Having cut down trees, split open the earth, and killed worms and insects,

children.text: karṣakaḥ khalayajñena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
children.translated_text: the farmer is released from all sins by the sacrifice of the threshing floor.

children.text: yo na dadyād dvijātibhyo rāśimūlam upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who does not give to the twice-born after he has reached the main heap of grain,

children.text: sa cauraḥ sa ca pāpiṣṭho brahmaghnaṃ taṃ vinirdiśet
children.translated_text: he is a thief, he is most sinful; one should declare him to be a slayer of a brahmin.

children.text: rājñe dattvā tu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ devānāṃ caikaviṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: But after giving a sixth part to the king, a twenty-first part to the gods,

children.text: viprāṇāṃ triṃśakaṃ bhāgaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
children.translated_text: and a thirtieth part to the brahmins, he is released from all sins.

children.text: kṣatriyo 'pi kṛṣiṃ kṛtvā devān viprāṃś ca pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: A kshatriya too, having practiced agriculture, should worship the gods and the brahmins.

children.text: vaiśyaḥ śūdras tathā kuryāt kṛṣivāṇijyaśilpakam
children.translated_text: A vaishya and a shudra should likewise practice agriculture, trade, and crafts.

children.text: vikarma kurvate śūdrā dvijaśuśrūṣayojjhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shudras who perform improper work, being devoid of service to the twice-born,

children.text: bhavanty alpāyuṣas te vai nirayaṃ yānty asaṃśayaṃ
children.translated_text: become short-lived and surely go to hell.

children.text: caturṇām api varṇānām eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the eternal <s>dharma</s> for all four varnas.

children.text: Chapter 3
ataḥ śuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi janane maraṇe tathā
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall explain purification in birth and also in death.

children.text: dinatrayeṇa śudhyanti brāhmaṇāḥ pretasūtake ||
children.translated_text: Brahmins become pure in three days in the impurity caused by a corpse.

children.text: kṣatriyo dvādaśāhena vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhakaiḥ
children.translated_text: A kshatriya becomes pure in twelve days, and a vaishya in fifteen days.

children.text: śūdraḥ śudhyati māsena parāśaravaco yathā ||
children.translated_text: A shudra becomes pure in a month, according to the word of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: upāsane tu viprāṇām aṅgaśuddhiś ca jāyate
children.translated_text: But through attendance upon brahmins, bodily purity also arises.

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ prasūtau tu dehasparśo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: At the birth of brahmins, bodily contact is prescribed.

children.text: jātau vipro daśāhena dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ
children.translated_text: At a birth, a brahmin becomes pure in ten days, a king in twelve days,

children.text: vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: a vaishya in fifteen days, and a shudra becomes pure in a month.

children.text: ekāhācchudhyate vipro yo 'gnivedasamanvitaḥ
children.translated_text: A brahmin who is furnished with the sacred fire and the Veda becomes pure after one day.

children.text: tryahāt kevalavedas tu dvihīno daśabhir dinaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who has only the Veda becomes pure after three days; one lacking both becomes pure in ten days.

children.text: janmakarmaparibhraṣṭaḥ saṃdhyopāsanavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: One who has fallen away from the rites of birth, and is without twilight worship,

children.text: nāmadhārakavipras tu daśāhaṃ sūtakī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: a brahmin in name only, is impure for ten days.

children.text: ekapiṇḍās tu dāyādāḥ pṛthagdāraniketanāḥ
children.translated_text: Heirs who share one funeral offering, though they have separate wives and dwellings,

children.text: janmany api vipattau ca teṣāṃ tat sūtakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: have that impurity both at birth and at misfortune.

children.text: tāvat tat sūtakaṃ gotre caturthapuruṣeṇa tu
children.translated_text: That impurity extends so far in the lineage, up to the fourth generation.

children.text: dāyād vicchedam āpnoti pañcamo vātmavaṃśajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The severance of heirship occurs with the fifth descendant in one's own line.

children.text: caturthe daśarātraṃ syāt ṣaṇṇiśāḥ puṃsi pañcame
children.translated_text: In the fourth generation there should be ten nights; in the fifth, six nights for a male.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe caturahācchuddhiḥ saptame tu dinatrayāt ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth there is purification after four days, and in the seventh after three days.

children.text: bhṛgvagnimaraṇe caiva deśāntaramṛte tathā
children.translated_text: In death by a fall, by fire, and likewise when death occurs in another country,

children.text: bāle prete ca saṃnyaste sadyaḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and when a child has died or one who has renounced has died, immediate purity is prescribed.

children.text: deśāntaramṛtaḥ kaścit sagotraḥ śrūyate yadi
children.translated_text: If it is heard that some kinsman of the same gotra has died in another country,

children.text: na trirātram ahorātraṃ sadyaḥ snātvā śucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: not three nights nor a full day and night are required; having bathed immediately, one becomes pure.

children.text: deśāntaragato vipraḥ prayāsāt kālakāritāt
children.translated_text: If a brahmin who has gone to another country, through travel and the working of time,

children.text: dehanāśam anuprāptas tithir na jñāyate yadi ||
children.translated_text: has met with destruction of the body, and the lunar date is not known,

children.text: kṛṣṇāṣṭamī tv amāvāsyā kṛṣṇā caikādaśī ca yā
children.translated_text: then on the dark eighth, on the new-moon day, or on the dark eleventh,

children.text: udakaṃ piṇḍadānaṃ ca tatra śrāddhaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: one should have water, the giving of rice-balls, and the śrāddha performed for him.

children.text: ajātadantā ye bālā ye ca garbhād viniḥsṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Children whose teeth have not yet appeared, and those who have come forth from the womb,

children.text: na teṣām agnisaṃskāro nāśaucaṃ nodakakriyā ||
children.translated_text: for them there is no cremation rite, no impurity, and no water-offering rite.

children.text: yadi garbho vipadyeta sravate vāpi yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: If a fetus should perish, or if it flows out from a woman,

children.text: yāvanmāsaṃ sthito garbho dinaṃ tāvat tu sūtakam ||
children.translated_text: for as many months as the fetus had remained, for that many days there is impurity.

children.text: ā caturthād bhavet srāvaḥ pātaḥ pañcamaṣaṣṭhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Up to the fourth month it is called a discharge; in the fifth and sixth it is a miscarriage.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ prasūtiḥ syād daśāhaṃ sūtakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: After that it is a delivery, and there is impurity for ten days.

children.text: dantajāte 'nujāte ca kṛtacūḍe ca saṃsthite
children.translated_text: When teeth have appeared, when birth has occurred, when the tonsure has been performed, and when the child has died,

children.text: agnisaṃskaraṇe teṣāṃ trirātram aśucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: at their cremation there is impurity for three nights.

children.text: ā dantajanmanaḥ sadya ā cūḍān naiṣṭhikī smṛtā
children.translated_text: Until the birth of teeth, purity is immediate; until the tonsure, it is remembered as final.

children.text: trirātram ā vratādeśād daśarātram ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: For three nights until the initiation into the vow, and after that for ten nights.

children.text: brahmacārī gṛhe yeṣāṃ hūyate ca hutāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: For those in whose house a brahmacarin is present and the sacrificial fire is offered,

children.text: saṃparkaṃ na ca kurvanti na teṣāṃ sūtakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if they do not make contact, there is no birth impurity for them.

children.text: saṃparkād duṣyate vipro janane maraṇe tathā
children.translated_text: A brahmin becomes defiled by contact, both at birth and at death.

children.text: saṃparkāc ca nivṛttasya na pretaṃ naiva sūtakam ||
children.translated_text: For one who has withdrawn from contact, there is neither corpse impurity nor birth impurity.

children.text: śilpinaḥ kārukā vaidyā dāsīdāsāś ca nāpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Artisans, craftsmen, physicians, female and male servants, and barbers,

children.text: rājānaḥ śrotriyāś caiva sadyaḥ śaucāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: kings and learned Vedic brahmins are declared to be immediately pure.

children.text: savrataḥ satrapūtaś ca āhitāgniś ca yo dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: A twice-born man who keeps vows, is purified by sacrifices, and maintains the sacred fires,

children.text: rājñaś ca sūtakaṃ nāsti yasya cecchati pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also a king: there is no birth impurity for one whom the ruler so wishes.

children.text: udyato nidhane dāne ārto vipro nimantritaḥ
children.translated_text: When one is engaged in death rites, in giving, when distressed, or when a brahmin has been invited,

children.text: tadaiva ṛṣibhir dṛṣṭaṃ yathā kālena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: then the sages have held that he becomes pure according to the proper time.

children.text: prasave gṛhamedhī tu na kuryāt saṃkaraṃ yadi
children.translated_text: At a delivery, if the householder does not mingle with her,

children.text: daśāhācchudhyate mātā tv avagāhya pitā śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mother becomes pure after ten days; the father, having bathed, is pure.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ śāvam āśaucaṃ mātāpitros tu sūtakam
children.translated_text: For all, corpse impurity applies; but for mother and father there is birth impurity.

children.text: sūtakaṃ mātur eva syād upaspṛśya pitā śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: Birth impurity belongs only to the mother; the father, after sipping water, is pure.

children.text: yadi patnyāṃ prasūtāyāṃ saṃparkaṃ kurute dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: If, when his wife has given birth, a twice-born man makes contact with her,

children.text: sūtakaṃ tu bhavet tasya yadi vipraḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit ||
children.translated_text: then birth impurity arises for him, even if he is a brahmin who knows the six auxiliaries of the Veda.

children.text: saṃparkāj jāyate doṣo nānyo doṣo 'sti vai dvije
children.translated_text: Fault arises from contact; there is no other fault for a twice-born man.

children.text: tasmāt sarvaprayatnena saṃparkaṃ varjayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise man should avoid contact with every effort.

children.text: vivāhotsavayajñeṣu tv antarā mṛtasūtake
children.translated_text: At weddings, festivals, and sacrifices, if corpse or birth impurity occurs in the midst,

children.text: pūrvasaṃkalpitaṃ dravyaṃ dīyamānaṃ na duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: the substance that had been previously resolved upon and is being given is not defiled.

children.text: antarā daśāhasya punar maraṇajanmanī
children.translated_text: If another death or birth occurs within the ten-day period,

children.text: tāvat syād aśucir vipro yāvat tat syād anirdaśam ||
children.translated_text: a brahmin remains impure only so long as that period has not completed its ten days.

children.text: brāhmaṇārthe vipannānāṃ bandigograhaṇe tathā
children.translated_text: For those who die for the sake of brahmins, and likewise in captivity or in the seizure of cattle,

children.text: āhaveṣu vipannānām ekarātram aśaucakam ||
children.translated_text: and for those who die in battles, there is impurity for one night.

children.text: dvāv imau puruṣau loke sūryamaṇḍalabhedinau
children.translated_text: These two men in the world pierce the disk of the sun:

children.text: parivrāḍ yogayuktaś ca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: a renouncer joined to yoga, and one killed while facing battle.

children.text: yatra yatra hataḥ śūraḥ śatrubhiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever a hero is killed, surrounded by enemies,

children.text: akṣayāṃl labhate lokān yadi klībaṃ na bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: he obtains imperishable worlds, if he does not speak as a coward.

children.text: saṃnyastaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthānāc calati bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: On seeing a brahmin who has renounced, the sun moves from its place, thinking,

children.text: eṣa me maṇḍalaṃ bhittvā paraṃ sthānaṃ prayāsyati ||
children.translated_text: 'This man will break through my orb and go to the supreme station.'

children.text: yas tu bhagneṣu sainyeṣu vidravatsu samantataḥ
children.translated_text: But when armies are broken and fleeing on every side,

children.text: paritrātā yadā gacchet sa ca kratuphalaṃ labhet ||
children.translated_text: if a rescuer then goes forth, he too obtains the fruit of a sacrifice.

children.text: yasya chedakṣataṃ gātraṃ śaramudgarayaṣṭibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The hero whose body is cut and wounded by arrows, clubs, and staffs,

children.text: devakanyās tu taṃ vīraṃ haranti ramayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: divine maidens carry him away and delight him.

children.text: devāṅganāsahasrāṇi śūram āyodhane hatam
children.translated_text: Thousands of divine women run hastily toward the hero slain in battle,

children.text: tvaramāṇāḥ pradhāvanti mama bhartā mameti ca ||
children.translated_text: each crying, 'He is my husband, mine!'

children.text: yaṃ yajñasaṃghais tapasā ca viprāḥ svargaiṣiṇo vātra yathā yānti
children.translated_text: The place to which brahmins seeking heaven go here by groups of sacrifices and by austerity,

children.text: kṣaṇena yānty eva hi tatra vīrāḥ prāṇān suyuddhena parityajantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there indeed heroes go in an instant, giving up their lives in a good battle.

children.text: jitena labhyate lakṣmīr mṛtenāpi surāṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: By victory wealth is obtained; even by death, heavenly women are obtained.

children.text: kṣaṇadhvaṃsini kāye 'smin kā cintā maraṇe raṇe ||
children.translated_text: In this body that perishes in a moment, what anxiety should there be about death in battle?

children.text: lalāṭadeśe rudhiraṃ sravac ca yasyāhave tu praviśec ca vaktram
children.translated_text: When blood flowing from the region of his forehead enters his mouth in combat,

children.text: tat somapānena kilāsya tulyaṃ saṃgrāmayajñe vidhivac ca dṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: that is said to be equal to his drinking soma, and is seen as proper in the sacrifice of battle.

children.text: anāthaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pretaṃ ye vahanti dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those twice-born men who carry a dead brahmin who is without protector,

children.text: pade pade yajñaphalam ānupūrvyāllabhanti te ||
children.translated_text: they obtain, step by step and in due order, the fruit of a sacrifice.

children.text: na teṣām aśubhaṃ kiṃcit pāpaṃ vā śubhakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: For those doers of good deeds there is no misfortune at all, nor any sin.

children.text: jalāvagāhanāt teṣāṃ sadyaḥśaucaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: For them immediate purity is prescribed through immersion in water.

children.text: asagotram abandhuṃ ca pretībhūtaṃ dvijottamam
children.translated_text: Having carried and cremated an excellent twice-born man who has died, who is not of one's gotra and is not a relative,

children.text: vahitvā ca dahitvā ca prāṇāyāmena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: one is purified by prāṇāyāma (breath-control).

children.text: anugamyecchayā pretaṃ jñātim ajñātim eva vā
children.translated_text: If one willingly follows a corpse, whether a known kinsman or an unknown person,

children.text: snātvā sacailaṃ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: after bathing with one's clothes on, touching fire, and eating ghee, one becomes purified.

children.text: kṣatriyaṃ mṛtam ajñānād brāhmaṇo yo 'nugacchati
children.translated_text: If a brahmin unknowingly follows a dead kṣatriya,

children.text: ekāham aśucir bhūtvā pañcagavyena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: after being impure for one day, he is purified by pañcagavya (the five products of the cow).

children.text: śavaṃ ca vaiśyam ajñānād brāhmaṇo yo 'nugacchati
children.translated_text: If a brahmin unknowingly follows the corpse of a vaiśya,

children.text: kṛtvāśaucaṃ dvirātraṃ ca prāṇāyāmān ṣaḍ ācaret ||
children.translated_text: after observing impurity for two nights, he should perform six prāṇāyāmas.

children.text: pretībhūtaṃ tu yaḥ śūdraṃ brāhmaṇo jñānadurbalaḥ
children.translated_text: But if a brahmin, weak in discernment, follows a śūdra who has died

children.text: anugacchen nīyamānaṃ trirātram aśucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: while the body is being carried away, he becomes impure for three nights.

children.text: trirātre tu tataḥ pūrṇe nadīṃ gatvā samudragām
children.translated_text: Then, when three nights have fully passed, he should go to a river that flows to the sea,

children.text: prāṇāyāmaśataṃ kṛtvā ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: perform one hundred prāṇāyāmas, eat ghee, and become purified.

children.text: vinirvartya yadā śūdrā udakāntam upasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: When śūdras have completed the rite and have come to the edge of the water,

children.text: dvijais tadānugantavyā eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then they are to be followed by twice-born men; this is the eternal dharma.

children.text: Chapter 4
atimānād atikrodhāt snehād vā yadi vā bhayāt
children.translated_text: If, from excessive pride, excessive anger, affection, or fear,

children.text: udbadhnīyāt strī pumān vā gatir eṣā vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: a woman or a man should hang himself or herself, this destination is prescribed:

children.text: pūyaśoṇitasampūrṇe tv andhe tamasi majjati
children.translated_text: that person sinks in blind darkness filled with pus and blood,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhīr varṣasahasrāṇi narakaṃ pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: and reaches hell for sixty thousand years.

children.text: nāśaucaṃ nodakaṃ nāgniṃ nāśrupātaṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: One should not cause impurity, water-offering, fire, or shedding of tears for such a person.

children.text: voḍhāro 'gnipradātāraḥ pāśacchedakarās tathā ||
children.translated_text: The bearers, the fire-givers, and also those who cut the noose,

children.text: taptakṛcchreṇa śudhyantīty evam āha prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: are purified by the taptakṛcchra penance; so said Prajāpati.

children.text: gobhir hataṃ tathodbaddhaṃ brāhmaṇena tu ghātitam ||
children.translated_text: So too for one killed by cows, one who has hanged himself, and one killed by a brahmin.

children.text: saṃspṛśanti tu ye viprā voḍhāraś cāgnidāś ca ye
children.translated_text: Those brahmins who touch them, and those who are bearers and fire-givers,

children.text: anye ye vānugantāraḥ pāśacchedakarāś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: and any others who follow them, and those who cut the noose,

children.text: taptakṛcchreṇa śuddhās te kuryur brāhmaṇabhojanam
children.translated_text: having been purified by taptakṛcchra, should feed brahmins.

children.text: anaḍutsahitāṃ gāṃ ca dadyur viprāya dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: They should also give as a fee to a brahmin a cow supported by a bull fit for breeding.

children.text: tryaham uṣṇaṃ pibed vāri tryaham uṣṇaṃ payaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: For three days one should drink hot water; for three days one should drink hot milk;

children.text: tryaham uṣṇaṃ pibet sarpir vāyubhakṣo dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: for three days one should drink hot ghee; for three days one should live on air.

children.text: ṣaṭpalaṃ tu pibed ambhas tripalaṃ tu payaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: One should drink six palas of water, three palas of milk,

children.text: palam ekaṃ pibet sarpis taptakṛcchraṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and one pala of ghee: this is prescribed as the taptakṛcchra.

children.text: yo vai samācared vipraḥ patitādiṣv akāmataḥ
children.translated_text: If a brahmin should have dealings unintentionally with fallen persons and the like

children.text: pañcāhaṃ vā daśāhaṃ vā dvādaśāham athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: for five days, ten days, or even twelve days,

children.text: māsārdhaṃ māsam ekaṃ vā māsadvayam athāpi vā
children.translated_text: for half a month, one month, or even two months,

children.text: abdārdham abdam ekaṃ vā tadūrdhvaṃ caiva tatsamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for half a year, one year, or beyond that, he becomes equal to them for that same duration.

children.text: trirātraṃ prathame pakṣe dvitīye kṛcchram ācaret
children.translated_text: In the first fortnight he should perform a three-night rite; in the second he should perform a kṛcchra penance.

children.text: tṛtīye caiva pakṣe tu kṛcchraṃ sāṃtapanaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: In the third fortnight he should perform the sāṃtapana kṛcchra.

children.text: caturthe daśarātraṃ syāt parākaḥ pañcame mataḥ
children.translated_text: In the fourth there should be a ten-night rite; in the fifth, the parāka is prescribed.

children.text: kuryāccāndrāyaṇaṃ ṣaṣṭhe saptame tv aindavadvayam ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth he should perform the cāndrāyaṇa; in the seventh, two aindava rites.

children.text: śuddhyartham aṣṭame caiva ṣaṇ māsān kṛcchram ācaret
children.translated_text: For purification in the eighth, he should perform kṛcchra for six months.

children.text: pakṣasaṃkhyāpramāṇena suvarṇāny api dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: As dakṣiṇā, he should also give gold pieces according to the number of fortnights.

children.text: ṛtusnātā tu yā nārī bhartāraṃ nopasarpati
children.translated_text: A woman who, after bathing at the end of her menstrual period, does not approach her husband

children.text: sā mṛtā narakaṃ yāti vidhavā ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes to hell when she dies and becomes a widow again and again.

children.text: ṛtusnātāṃ tu yo bhāryāṃ saṃnidhau nopagacchati
children.translated_text: A man who does not approach his wife, bathed after menstruation, when she is near,

children.text: ghorāyāṃ bhrūṇahatyāyāṃ yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is joined to the terrible sin of killing an embryo; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: daridraṃ vyādhitaṃ mūrkhaṃ bhartāraṃ yāvamanyate
children.translated_text: A woman who disrespects her husband because he is poor, sick, or foolish,

children.text: sā śunī jāyate mṛtvā sūkarī ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after death is born as a bitch and again and again as a sow.

children.text: patyau jīvati yā nārī upoṣya vratam ācaret
children.translated_text: A woman who observes a fast or vow while her husband is alive

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ harate bhartuḥ sā nārī narakaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: takes away her husband's lifespan; that woman goes to hell.

children.text: apṛṣṭvā caiva bhartāraṃ yā nārī kurute vratam
children.translated_text: And whatever vow a woman undertakes without asking her husband,

children.text: sarvaṃ tad rākṣasān gacched ity evaṃ manur abravīt ||
children.translated_text: all that goes to the rākṣasas; so Manu declared.

children.text: bāndhavānāṃ sajātīnāṃ durvṛttaṃ kurute tu yā
children.translated_text: A woman who behaves wickedly toward relatives and those of her own class,

children.text: garbhapātaṃ ca yā kuryān na tāṃ saṃbhāṣayet kvacit ||
children.translated_text: and a woman who causes a miscarriage, one should never speak with her.

children.text: yat pāpaṃ brahmahatyāyāṃ dviguṇaṃ garbhapātane
children.translated_text: The sin that belongs to killing a brahmin is doubled in abortion.

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ na tasyāḥ syāt tasyās tyāgo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: There should be no penance for her; abandonment of her is prescribed.

children.text: na kāryam āvasathyena nāgnihotreṇa vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: No rite is to be performed again with the domestic fire or with the agnihotra.

children.text: sa bhavet karmacāṇḍālo yas tu dharmaparāṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who has turned away from <s>dharma</s> becomes a ritual outcaste in his acts.

children.text: oghavātāhṛtaṃ bījaṃ yasya kṣetre prarohati
children.translated_text: When seed carried off by a flood or wind sprouts in someone’s field,

children.text: sa kṣetrī labhate bījaṃ na bījī bhāgam arhati ||
children.translated_text: the owner of the field receives the seed; the sower of the seed is not entitled to a share.

children.text: tadvat parastriyāḥ putrau dvau smṛtau kuṇḍagolakau
children.translated_text: In the same way, two sons of another man’s wife are remembered as the kuṇḍa and the golaka.

children.text: patyau jīvati kuṇḍaḥ syāt mṛte bhartari golakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While the husband is living he is called a kuṇḍa; when the husband is dead, a golaka.

children.text: aurasaḥ kṣetrajaś caiva dattaḥ kṛtrimakaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: There is the body-born son, the son begotten on the wife, the given son, and the made son.

children.text: dadyān mātā pitā vāpi sa putro dattako bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Whom the mother or father gives, he is to be regarded as an adopted son.

children.text: parivittiḥ parivettā yayā ca parividyate
children.translated_text: The younger brother who marries first, the elder brother who is passed over, and the woman by whom the passing-over occurs,

children.text: sarve te narakaṃ yānti dātṛyājakapañcamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all these go to hell, with the giver and the officiating priest as the fifth.

children.text: dvau kṛcchrau parivittes tu kanyāyāḥ kṛcchra eva ca
children.translated_text: For the younger brother who marries first there are two kṛcchra penances, and for the maiden one kṛcchra.

children.text: kṛcchrātikṛcchrau dātus tu hotā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: For the giver there are the kṛcchra and atikṛcchra penances, while the hotṛ should perform a cāndrāyaṇa.

children.text: kubjavāmanaṣaṇḍheṣu gadgadeṣu jaḍeṣu ca
children.translated_text: In the case of hunchbacks, dwarfs, impotent men, stammerers, and dull-witted men,

children.text: jātyandhe badhire mūke na doṣaḥ parivedane ||
children.translated_text: and those blind from birth, deaf, or mute, there is no fault in passing them over.

children.text: pitṛvyaputraḥ sāpatnaḥ paranārīsutas tathā
children.translated_text: A paternal uncle’s son, a son of a co-wife, and likewise a son of another woman:

children.text: dārāgnihotrasaṃyoge na doṣaḥ parivedane ||
children.translated_text: in connection with marriage and the agnihotra, there is no fault in passing them over.

children.text: jyeṣṭho bhrātā yadā tiṣṭhed ādhānaṃ naiva kārayet
children.translated_text: When the elder brother remains unmarried, one should not have the establishment of the sacred fire performed.

children.text: anujñātas tu kurvīta śaṅkhasya vacanaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: But when permitted by him, one may do it, according to the statement of <s>Śaṅkha</s>.

children.text: naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe ca patite patau
children.translated_text: When the husband is lost, dead, has renounced, is impotent, or fallen,

children.text: pañcasv āpatsu nārīṇāṃ patir anyo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: in these five emergencies another husband is prescribed for women.

children.text: mṛte bhartari yā nārī brahmacaryavrate sthitā
children.translated_text: A woman who, when her husband is dead, remains in a vow of chastity,

children.text: sā mṛtā labhate svargaṃ yathā te brahmacāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on dying obtains heaven, just like those brahmacārins.

children.text: tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdhakoṭī ca yāni romāṇi mānuṣe
children.translated_text: As many hairs as there are on a human body, three and a half crores,

children.text: tāvatkālaṃ vaset svarge bhartāraṃ yānugacchati ||
children.translated_text: for that long she dwells in heaven, if she follows her husband.

children.text: vyālagrāhī yathā vyālaṃ balād uddharate bilāt
children.translated_text: Just as a snake-catcher forcibly draws a snake out of its hole,

children.text: evaṃ strī patim uddhṛtya tenaiva saha modate ||
children.translated_text: so a woman, having lifted up her husband, rejoices together with him.

children.text: Chapter 5
vṛkaśvānasṛgālādyair daṣṭo yas tu dvijottamaḥ
children.translated_text: If an excellent twice-born man is bitten by a wolf, dog, jackal, or the like,

children.text: snātvā japet sa gāyatrīṃ pavitrāṃ vedamātaram ||
children.translated_text: after bathing he should recite the sacred Gāyatrī, mother of the Veda.

children.text: gavāṃ śṛṅgodakaiḥ snānaṃ mahānadyos tu saṃgame
children.translated_text: By bathing with water from a cow’s horn, at the confluence of great rivers,

children.text: samudradarśanād vāpi śunā daṣṭaḥ śucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: or even by seeing the ocean, one bitten by a dog becomes pure.

children.text: vedavidyāvratasnātaḥ śunā daṣṭo dvijo yadi
children.translated_text: If a twice-born man learned in the Veda and purified by vows and bath is bitten by a dog,

children.text: sa hiraṇyodakaiḥ snātvā ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: having bathed with gold-infused water and eaten ghee, he is purified.

children.text: savratas tu śunā daṣṭo yas trirātram upāvaset
children.translated_text: But if one under a vow is bitten by a dog, he should fast for three nights;

children.text: ghṛtaṃ kuśodakaṃ pītvā vrataśeṣaṃ samāpayet ||
children.translated_text: after drinking ghee and kuśa-water, he should complete the remainder of his vow.

children.text: avrataḥ savrato vāpi śunā daṣṭo bhaved dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether not under a vow or under a vow, if a twice-born man is bitten by a dog,

children.text: praṇipatya bhavet pūto vipraiś cakṣurnirīkṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he becomes purified by bowing down and being seen with the eyes by brahmins.

children.text: śunā ghrātāvalīḍhasya nakhair vilikhitasya ca
children.translated_text: For one smelled, licked, or scratched with the nails by a dog,

children.text: adbhiḥ prakṣālanaṃ proktam agninā copacūlanam ||
children.translated_text: washing with water is prescribed, and also warming by fire.

children.text: śunā tu brāhmaṇī daṣṭā jambukena vṛkeṇa vā
children.translated_text: If a brahmin woman is bitten by a dog, a jackal, or a wolf,

children.text: uditaṃ grahanakṣatraṃ dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ śucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: having seen a risen planet or constellation, she immediately becomes pure.

children.text: kṛṣṇapakṣe yadā somo na dṛśyeta kadācana
children.translated_text: When the moon is never visible in the dark fortnight,

children.text: yāṃ diśaṃ vrajate somas tāṃ diśaṃ vāvalokayet ||
children.translated_text: one should look toward the direction in which the moon goes.

children.text: asadbrāhmaṇake grāme śunā daṣṭo dvijottamaḥ
children.translated_text: If an excellent twice-born man is bitten by a dog in a village without good brahmins,

children.text: vṛṣaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sadyaḥ snātvā śucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: having circumambulated a bull and bathed immediately, he becomes pure.

children.text: caṇḍālena śvapākena gobhir viprair hato yadi
children.translated_text: If an āhitāgni brahmin is killed by a caṇḍāla, a dog-cooker, cows, or brahmins,

children.text: āhitāgnir mṛto vipro viṣeṇātmahato yadi ||
children.translated_text: or if that brahmin dies from poison or by suicide,

children.text: dahet taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vipro lokāgnau mantravarjitam
children.translated_text: a brahmin should burn that brahmin in ordinary fire, without mantras.

children.text: spṛṣṭvā voḍhvā ca dagdhvā ca sapiṇḍeṣu ca sarvathā ||
children.translated_text: After touching, carrying, and burning him, and in every case among the sapiṇḍas,

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ caret paścād viprāṇām anuśāsanāt
children.translated_text: one should afterward perform a prājāpatya penance, according to the instruction of brahmins.

children.text: dagdhāsthīni punar gṛhya kṣīraiḥ prakṣālayed dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking up the burned bones again, the twice-born man should wash them with milk.

children.text: punar dahet svāgninā tu svatantreṇa pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: Then he should burn them again, separately and independently, with his own sacred fire.

children.text: āhitāgnir dvijaḥ kaścit pravasan kālacoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If some twice-born āhitāgni, while living abroad and driven by time,

children.text: dehanāśam anuprāptas tasyāgnir vasate gṛhe
children.translated_text: has come to the destruction of the body, while his fire remains at home,

children.text: pretāgnihotrasaṃskāraḥ śrūyatām ṛṣipuṅgavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: listen to the rite of the funeral agnihotra, O best of seers.

children.text: kṛṣṇājinaṃ samāstīrya kuśais tu puruṣākṛtim
children.translated_text: Having spread a black antelope skin, one should make a human form with kuśa grass.

children.text: ṣaṭśatāni śataṃ caiva palāśānāṃ ca vṛntataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There should be six hundred and one hundred stalks of palāśa wood.

children.text: catvāriṃśacchire dadyācchataṃ kaṇṭhe tu vinyaset
children.translated_text: He should put forty at the head, and place one hundred at the neck.

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ śatakaṃ dadyād aṅgulīṣu daśaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: He should put one hundred at the two arms, and just ten on the fingers.

children.text: śataṃ tu jaghane dadyād dviśataṃ tūdare tathā
children.translated_text: He should put one hundred at the hips, and likewise two hundred at the belly.

children.text: dadyād aṣṭau vṛṣaṇayoḥ pañca meḍhre tu vinyaset ||
children.translated_text: He should put eight at the testicles and place five at the penis.

children.text: ekaviṃśatim ūrubhyāṃ dviśataṃ jānujaṅghayoḥ
children.translated_text: Twenty-one should be put at the two thighs, and two hundred at the knees and shanks.

children.text: pādāṅgulīṣu ṣaḍ dadyād yajñapātraṃ tato nyaset ||
children.translated_text: He should put six at the toes; then he should set down the sacrificial vessel.

children.text: śamyāṃ śiśne viniḥkṣipya araṇīṃ muṣkayor api
children.translated_text: Putting the śamyā at the penis and the araṇi pieces also at the testicles,

children.text: juhūṃ ca dakṣiṇe haste vāme tūpabhṛtaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: he should place the juhū in the right hand and the upabhṛt in the left.

children.text: karṇe colūkhalaṃ dadyāt pṛṣṭhe ca musalaṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: He should put the mortar at the ear and place the pestle on the back.

children.text: urasi kṣipya dṛṣadaṃ taṇḍulājyatilān mukhe ||
children.translated_text: Having put the grinding stone on the chest, he should place rice, ghee, and sesame in the mouth.

children.text: śrotre ca prokṣaṇīṃ dadyād ājyasthalīṃ tu cakṣuṣoḥ
children.translated_text: He should put the sprinkling vessel at the ear, and the ghee-vessel at the two eyes.

children.text: karṇe netre mukhe ghrāṇe hiraṇyaśakalaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: At the ears, eyes, mouth, and nose he should place a piece of gold.

children.text: agnihotropakaraṇam aśeṣaṃ tatra nikṣipet
children.translated_text: All the implements of the agnihotra should be deposited there without remainder.

children.text: asau svargāya lokāya svāhety ekāhutiṃ sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Saying, “svāhā to that heavenly world,” he should offer one oblation once.

children.text: dadyāt putro 'thavā bhrātāpy anyo vāpi ca bāndhavaḥ
children.translated_text: The son should offer it, or the brother too, or some other relative.

children.text: yathā dahanasaṃskāras tathā kāryaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the cremation rite is, so it should be performed by the wise.

children.text: īdṛśaṃ tu vidhiṃ kuryād brahmalokagatiḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: One should perform such a rite; it is remembered to lead to the world of Brahmā.

children.text: dahanti ye dvijās taṃ tu te yānti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: The twice-born men who burn him go to the highest state.

children.text: anyathā kurvate karma tv ātmabuddhyā pracoditāḥ
children.translated_text: But those who perform the act otherwise, impelled by their own judgment,

children.text: bhavanty alpāyuṣas te vai patanti narake 'śucau ||
children.translated_text: become short-lived indeed, and they fall into an impure hell.

children.text: Chapter 6
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi prāṇihatyāsu niṣkṛtim
children.translated_text: After this I shall declare the expiation for the killing of living beings,

children.text: parāśarena pūrvoktā manvarthe 'pi ca vistṛtām ||
children.translated_text: previously taught by <s>Parāśara</s> and also expanded for the purpose of the <s>Manu</s> tradition.

children.text: krauñcasārasahaṃsāṃś ca cakravākaṃ ca kukkuṭam
children.translated_text: For killing a krauñca, a sārasa, a goose, a cakravāka, and a cock,

children.text: jālapādaṃ ca śarabham ahorātreṇa śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: and a jālapāda and a śarabha, one is purified in a day and night.

children.text: balākāṭiṭṭibhau vāpi śukapārāvatāv api
children.translated_text: For a balākā and a ṭiṭṭibha, or also a parrot and a pigeon,

children.text: ahinakravighātī ca śudhyate naktabhojanāt ||
children.translated_text: and for one who kills a snake, a crocodile, or the like, one is purified by eating only at night.

children.text: vṛkakākakapotānāṃ śāritittirighātakaḥ
children.translated_text: The killer of wolves, crows, and doves, and of śāri birds and partridges,

children.text: antarjala ubhe saṃdhye prāṇāyāmena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: standing in water at both twilights, is purified by breath-control.

children.text: gṛdhraśyenaśaśādānām ulūkasya ca ghātakaḥ
children.translated_text: The killer of vultures, hawks, hares, and owls

children.text: apakvāśī dinaṃ tiṣṭhet trikālaṃ mārutāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should remain for a day eating uncooked food and, at the three times of day, subsisting on air.

children.text: valguṇīṭiṭṭibhānāṃ ca kokilākhañjarīṭake
children.translated_text: For valguṇī birds and ṭiṭṭibhas, and for cuckoos and khañjarīṭakas,

children.text: lāvikāraktapakṣeṣu śudhyate naktabhojanāt ||
children.translated_text: and for lāvikās and red-winged birds, one is purified by eating only at night.

children.text: kāraṇḍavacakorāṇāṃ piṅgalākurarasya ca
children.translated_text: For killing kāraṇḍavas and cakoras, and the piṅgala and kurara,

children.text: bhāradvājādikaṃ hatvā śivaṃ pūjya viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: and such birds as the bhāradvāja, one becomes purified after worshiping <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: bheruṇḍacāṣabhāsāṃś ca pārāvatakapiñjalau
children.translated_text: For bheruṇḍas, cāṣas, and bhāsas, and for pigeons and kapiñjalas,

children.text: pakṣiṇāṃ caiva sarveṣām ahorātram abhojanam ||
children.translated_text: and indeed for all birds, there is fasting for a day and night.

children.text: hatvā mūṣakamārjārasarpājagaraḍuṇḍubhān
children.translated_text: Having killed mice, cats, snakes, pythons, and ḍuṇḍubha snakes,

children.text: kṛsaraṃ bhojayed viprān lohadaṇḍaś ca dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: one should feed brahmins with kṛsara, and the fee is an iron staff.

children.text: śiśumāraṃ tathā godhāṃ hatvā kūrmaṃ ca śalyakam
children.translated_text: Having killed a śiśumāra, likewise an iguana, a tortoise, or a porcupine,

children.text: vṛntākaphalabhakṣī cāpyahorātreṇa śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: one who eats eggplant fruit is purified in a day and night.

children.text: vṛkajambūkaṛkṣāṇāṃ tarakṣuśvānaghātakaḥ
children.translated_text: The killer of a wolf, jackal, bear, tarakṣu, or dog

children.text: tilaprasthaṃ dvije dadyād vāyubhakṣo dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: should give a prastha of sesame to a twice-born man and subsist on air for three days.

children.text: gajasya ca turaṅgasya mahiṣoṣṭranipātane
children.translated_text: For the killing of an elephant, a horse, a buffalo, or a camel,

children.text: prāyaścittam ahorātraṃ trisaṃdhyam avagāhanam ||
children.translated_text: the expiation is a day and night with immersion at the three twilights.

children.text: kuraṅgaṃ vānaraṃ siṃhaṃ citraṃ vyāghraṃ tu ghātayan
children.translated_text: When one kills an antelope, a monkey, a lion, a spotted deer, or a tiger,

children.text: śudhyate sa trirātreṇa viprāṇāṃ tarpaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: he is purified in three nights, and by satisfying brahmins.

children.text: mṛgarohidvarāhāṇām aver bastasya ghātakaḥ
children.translated_text: The killer of deer, rohita deer, boars, sheep, or goats

children.text: aphālakṛṣṭam aśnīyād ahorātram upoṣya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: should eat what has grown in unploughed ground, after fasting for a day and night.

children.text: evaṃ catuṣpadānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vanacāriṇām
children.translated_text: Thus also for all quadrupeds that roam in the forest,

children.text: ahorātroṣitas tiṣṭhej japed vai jātavedasam ||
children.translated_text: one should remain fasting for a day and night and recite the hymn to <s>Jātavedas</s>.

children.text: śilpinaṃ kārukaṃ śūdraṃ striyaṃ vā yas tu ghātayet
children.translated_text: Whoever kills an artisan, a craftsman, a śūdra, or a woman

children.text: prājāpatyadvayaṃ kṛtvā vṛṣaikādaśadakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: should perform two prājāpatya penances, with eleven bulls as the sacrificial fee.

children.text: vaiśyaṃ vā kṣatriyaṃ vāpi nirdoṣaṃ yo 'bhighātayet
children.translated_text: Whoever strikes down an innocent vaiśya or kṣatriya

children.text: so 'pi kṛcchradvayaṃ kuryād goviṃśaddakṣiṇāṃ dadet ||
children.translated_text: should also perform two kṛcchra penances and give twenty cows as the fee.

children.text: vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ kriyāsaktaṃ vikarmasthaṃ dvijottamam
children.translated_text: Having killed a vaiśya, a śūdra intent on ritual acts, or an excellent twice-born man engaged in wrong action,

children.text: hatvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ tasya triṃśad goś caiva dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: the penance for him is a cāndrāyaṇa, and thirty cows as the fee.

children.text: caṇḍālaṃ hatavān kaścid brāhmaṇe yadi kaṃcana
children.translated_text: If someone has killed a caṇḍāla in relation to a brahmin,

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ caret kṛcchraṃ godvayaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadat ||
children.translated_text: he should undertake a prājāpatya kṛcchra, giving two cows as the fee.

children.text: kṣatriyeṇāpi vaiśyena śūdreṇaivetareṇa vā
children.translated_text: When the killing of a caṇḍāla has been committed by a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, a śūdra, or another,

children.text: caṇḍālasya vadhe prāpte kṛcchrārdhena viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: he is purified by half a kṛcchra penance.

children.text: corau śvapākacaṇḍālau vipreṇābhihatau yadi
children.translated_text: If thieves, śvapākas, or caṇḍālas are struck down by a brahmin,

children.text: ahorātroṣitaḥ snātvā pañcagavyena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: he is purified by fasting for a day and night, bathing, and taking pañcagavya.

children.text: śvapākaṃ vāpi caṇḍālaṃ vipraḥ sambhāṣate yadi
children.translated_text: If a brahmin speaks with a śvapāka or a caṇḍāla,

children.text: dvijasaṃbhāṣaṇaṃ kuryāt sāvitrīṃ tu sakṛj japet ||
children.translated_text: he should converse with a twice-born man and recite the Sāvitrī once.

children.text: caṇḍālaiḥ saha suptaṃ tu trirātram upavāsayet
children.translated_text: One who has slept together with caṇḍālas should be made to fast for three nights.

children.text: caṇḍālaikapathaṃ gatvā gāyatrīsmaraṇācchuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gone on a single road with a caṇḍāla, he is pure by remembering the Gāyatrī.

children.text: caṇḍāladarśane sadya ādityam avalokayet
children.translated_text: On seeing a caṇḍāla, one should at once look at the sun.

children.text: caṇḍālasparśane caiva sacailaṃ snānam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: And on touching a caṇḍāla, one should bathe together with one's clothes.

children.text: caṇḍālakhātavāpīṣu pītvā salilam agrajaḥ
children.translated_text: If a twice-born elder drinks water from wells or tanks dug by caṇḍālas,

children.text: ajñānāccaikabhaktena tv ahorātreṇa śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: then, if it was through ignorance, he is purified by one meal and by a day and night.

children.text: caṇḍālabhāṇḍasaṃspṛṣṭaṃ pītvā kūpagataṃ jalam
children.translated_text: Having drunk well-water touched by a caṇḍāla's vessel,

children.text: gomūtrayāvakāhāras trirātrācchuddhim āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: one obtains purity after three nights on a diet of cow urine and barley gruel.

children.text: caṇḍālaghaṭasaṃsthaṃ tu yat toyaṃ pibati dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: When a twice-born man drinks water that has been kept in a caṇḍāla's pot,

children.text: tatkṣaṇāt kṣipate yas tu prājāpatyaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: if he spits it out at once, he should perform a prājāpatya penance.

children.text: yadi na kṣipate toyaṃ śarīre yasya jīryati
children.translated_text: If he does not spit out the water and it is digested in his body,

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ na dātavyaṃ kṛcchraṃ sāṃtapanaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: a prājāpatya is not to be prescribed; he should perform a sāṃtapana kṛcchra.

children.text: caret sāṃtapanaṃ vipraḥ prājāpatyam anantaraḥ
children.translated_text: A brahmin should perform a sāṃtapana, and next a prājāpatya.

children.text: tadardhaṃ tu cared vaiśyaḥ pādaṃ śūdras tad ācaret ||
children.translated_text: A vaiśya should perform half of that, and a śūdra should perform a quarter of it.

children.text: bhāṇḍastham antyajānāṃ tu jalaṃ dadhi payaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: If a brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, or śūdra through negligence drinks

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdraś caiva pramādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: water, curds, or milk kept in the vessel of antyajas,

children.text: brahmakūrcopavāsena dvijātīnāṃ tu niṣkṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: the expiation for the twice-born is fasting with brahmakūrca;

children.text: śūdrasya copavāsena tathā dānena śaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a śūdra it is fasting, and likewise giving according to his ability.

children.text: bhuṅkte 'jñānād dvijaśreṣṭhaś caṇḍālānnaṃ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: If an excellent twice-born man somehow eats caṇḍāla food unknowingly,

children.text: gomūtrayāvakāhāro daśarātreṇa śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: he is purified in ten nights by a diet of cow urine and barley gruel.

children.text: ekaikaṃ grāsam aśnīyād gomūtrayāvakasya ca
children.translated_text: He should eat one morsel at a time of the cow-urine barley gruel.

children.text: daśāhaṃ niyamasthasya vrataṃ tat tu vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: For one who remains under discipline for ten days, that is prescribed as the vow.

children.text: avijñātas tu caṇḍālo yatra veśmani tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Where an unrecognized caṇḍāla stays in a house,

children.text: vijñāte tūpasannasya dvijāḥ kurvanty anugraham ||
children.translated_text: when he is recognized, twice-born men who have approached it perform an act of grace.

children.text: munivaktrodgatān dharmān gāyanto vedapāragāḥ
children.translated_text: Singing the dharmas that have issued from the mouth of the sage, those who have mastered the Veda,

children.text: patantam uddhareyus taṃ dharmajñāḥ pāpasaṃkarāt ||
children.translated_text: being knowers of dharma, should lift him as he is falling from the mixture of sin.

children.text: dadhnā ca sarpiṣā caiva kṣīragomūtrayāvakam
children.translated_text: With curds and with ghee, milk, cow urine, and barley gruel,

children.text: bhuñjīta saha sarvaiś ca trisaṃdhyam avagāhanam ||
children.translated_text: he should eat together with all, and immerse himself at the three twilights.

children.text: tryahaṃ bhuñjīta dadhnā ca tryahaṃ bhuñjīta sarpiṣā
children.translated_text: For three days he should eat with curds, and for three days he should eat with ghee.

children.text: tryahaṃ kṣīreṇa bhuñjīta ekaikena dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: For three days he should eat with milk, each one for a period of three days.

children.text: bhāvaduṣṭaṃ na bhuñjīta nocchiṣṭaṃ kṛmidūṣitam
children.translated_text: One should not eat food spoiled in its condition, nor leftovers contaminated by worms.

children.text: dadhikṣīrasya tripalaṃ palaṃ ekaṃ ghṛtasya tu ||
children.translated_text: For curds and milk there are three palas, but for ghee there is one pala.

children.text: bhasmanā tu bhavecchuddhir ubhayos tāmrakāṃsyayoḥ
children.translated_text: By ashes there is purification of both copper and bronze vessels.

children.text: jalaśaucena vastrāṇāṃ parityāgena mṛṇmayam ||
children.translated_text: Cloths are purified by washing with water; earthenware is purified by being discarded.

children.text: kusumbhaguḍakārpāsalavaṇaṃ tailasarpiṣī
children.translated_text: Safflower, molasses, cotton, salt, oil, and ghee,

children.text: dvāre kṛtvā tu dhānyāni dadyād veśmani pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: and grains should be placed at the doorway, and fire should be given in the dwelling.

children.text: evaṃ śuddhas tataḥ paścāt kuryād brāhmaṇatarpaṇam
children.translated_text: Thus purified, afterward one should perform the satisfaction of brahmins.

children.text: triṃśataṃ govṛṣaṃ caikaṃ dadyād vipreṣu dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: One should give thirty cows and one bull as a fee among the brahmins.

children.text: punar lepanakhātena homajapyena śudhyati
children.translated_text: Again, by smearing, digging out, oblation, and recitation it becomes pure.

children.text: ādhāreṇa ca viprāṇāṃ bhūmidoṣo na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: And through the support of brahmins there is no fault in the ground.

children.text: caṇḍālaiḥ saha saṃparkaṃ māsaṃ māsārdham eva vā
children.translated_text: If there has been association with caṇḍālas for a month, or even for half a month,

children.text: gomūtrayāvakāhāro māsārdhena viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: one who lives on cow urine and barley gruel is purified in half a month.

children.text: rajakī carmakārī ca lubdhakī veṇujīvinī
children.translated_text: A washerwoman, a leather-worker woman, a huntress, and a woman living by bamboo-work,

children.text: cāturvarṇyasya ca gṛhe tv avijñātā tu tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: if she remains unknown in the house of one of the four varṇas,

children.text: jñātvā tu niṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt pūrvoktasyārdham eva ca
children.translated_text: then, when it is known, one should perform an expiation, namely half of what was stated before.

children.text: gṛhadāhaṃ na kurvīta śeṣaṃ sarvaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: One should not burn the house; all the rest should be carried out.

children.text: gṛhasyābhyantaraṃ gaccheccaṇḍālo yadi kasyacit
children.translated_text: If a caṇḍāla enters the inside of someone's house,

children.text: tam agārād vinirvāsya mṛdbhāṇḍaṃ tu visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: having expelled him from the house, one should throw away the earthen vessel.

children.text: rasapūrṇaṃ tu yad bhāṇḍaṃ na tyajet tu kadācana
children.translated_text: But a vessel filled with liquid should never be discarded.

children.text: gomayena tu saṃmiśrair jalaiḥ prokṣed gṛhaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: One should sprinkle the house with waters mixed with cow dung in the same way.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya vraṇadvāre pūyaśoṇitasaṃbhave
children.translated_text: When, in the opening of a brahmin's wound, pus and blood have arisen,

children.text: kṛmir utpadyate yasya prāyaścittaṃ kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and worms are produced in him, how is the expiation to be?

children.text: gavāṃ mūtrapurīṣeṇa dadhnā kṣīreṇa sarpiṣā
children.translated_text: With the urine and dung of cows, with curds, milk, and ghee,

children.text: tryahaṃ snātvā ca pītvā ca kṛmiduṣṭaḥ śucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: having bathed and drunk for three days, one defiled by worms becomes pure.

children.text: kṣatriyo 'pi suvarṇasya pañcamāṣān pradāya tu
children.translated_text: For a kṣatriya too, after he has given five māṣas of gold,

children.text: godakṣiṇāṃ tu vaiśyasyāpy upavāsaṃ vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: one should prescribe a cow as the fee for a vaiśya too, and fasting.

children.text: śūdrāṇāṃ nopavāsaḥ syācchūdro dānena śudhyati
children.translated_text: For śūdras there should be no fast; a śūdra is purified by giving.

children.text: acchidram iti yad vākyaṃ vadanti kṣitidevatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The statement 'without a breach,' which the gods on earth declare,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā grāhyam agniṣṭomaphalaṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: is to be accepted with the head bowed down, for it has the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

children.text: japacchidraṃ tapacchidraṃ yacchidraṃ yajñakarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: A breach in recitation, a breach in austerity, whatever breach occurs in the rite of sacrifice,

children.text: sarvaṃ bhavati niśchidraṃ brāhmaṇair upapāditam
children.translated_text: all becomes without breach when it is confirmed by brahmins.

children.text: vyādhivyasaniniśrānte durbhikṣe ḍāmare tathā ||
children.translated_text: For one exhausted by illness or calamity, in famine or in disorder,

children.text: upavāso vrataṃ homo dvijasampāditāni vai
children.translated_text: fasting, a vow, and oblation are indeed to be completed by twice-born men.

children.text: athavā brāhmaṇās tuṣṭāḥ sarvaṃ kurvanty anugraham ||
children.translated_text: Or, when brahmins are satisfied, they grant favor in every matter.

children.text: sarvān kāmān avāpnoti dvijasampāditair iha
children.translated_text: One obtains all desires here through what has been completed by twice-born men.

children.text: durbale 'nugrahaḥ proktas tathā vai bālavṛddhayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Favor is prescribed for a weak person, and likewise for a child or an old man.

children.text: ato 'nyathā bhaved doṣas tasmān nānugrahaḥ smṛtaḥ
